column3: Description
The main, high‑emphasis button used for a page’s single most important action.
Lower‑emphasis button that accompanies the primary action (e.g., “Cancel”).
Square button with both icon and text, ideal for toolbar actions.
Round or square button that shows just an icon to save space.
Combines a primary action on the left with a dropdown arrow on the right for extra options.
Button that opens a menu of additional commands when clicked.
Button that stays pressed or unpressed, representing on/off states.
Group of adjacent buttons where only one can be active at a time.
Circular button hovering over content—commonly used for “Add” on mobile.
Two or more related buttons placed side‑by‑side with shared borders.
Horizontal row of grouped buttons forming a compact action bar.
Horizontal trail of links showing the user’s current location hierarchy.
Top bar containing primary navigation links across the width of the page.
Tall column of links on the left or right side for section switching.
Collapsed three‑line icon that expands into a full navigation drawer on tap.
Wide hover menu displaying multiple link columns, images, or promos.
Nested menu that appears on hover or click beside its parent item.
Small pop‑up list of actions tied to a specific element or selection.
Centered overlay input that lets users type to execute any command quickly.
Off‑canvas panel that slides in from the side to reveal navigation links.
Fixed bar with 3‑5 icons at the bottom of a mobile viewport.
“Previous,” page numbers, and “Next” buttons for stepping through data pages.
Automatically fetches more content as the user nears the list’s end.
Manual trigger that appends another batch of list items below.
Row of numbered circles guiding users through sequential steps.
Linear bar showing current step and remaining steps in a multi‑page flow.
Row of tab labels that switch between different content panels.
Tab labels stacked vertically, useful when horizontal space is limited.
Rounded pill‑style tabs offering a softer alternative to square tabs.
Last breadcrumb segment includes a dropdown to jump among sibling pages.
Sidebar links highlight as the user scrolls past corresponding page sections.
Small floating button that appears after scrolling, returning users to page top.
Bar with primary actions that sticks to top or bottom once the user scrolls past hero.
FAB expands into several mini‑action buttons when tapped.
Three‑dot icon revealing less‑frequent actions in a compact list.
Swiping a mobile list row reveals contextual actions like delete or archive.
Dragging down on a list triggers a refresh animation and data reload.
Edge swipe on mobile returns the user to the previous screen.
Shows key‑combo hints beside buttons when the user presses “?” or similar.
Hidden link that appears on focus, letting keyboard users jump past nav.
Left/right arrows flanking a carousel for manual slide control.
Small dots or mini images indicating slide position and enabling quick jumps.
Clicking a header expands or collapses its content beneath.
Small triangular icon that rotates to show hidden details inline.
One‑click control toggles every accordion section simultaneously.
Pencil or edit icon appears on hover, enabling quick field editing.
“⋯” button inside a table row revealing actions specific to that row.
Appears when multiple items are selected, offering mass delete, move, etc.
Temporary toast message with an “Undo” button after a destructive action.
Toast notification featuring a secondary link, e.g., “View details.”
A mini row of icons that fades in near selected text or images, offering quick actions like copy or bold.
Expandable nested list that lets users drill into multi‑level sections without leaving the sidebar.
Collapses middle breadcrumb segments into “…”; clicking reveals the hidden path for long hierarchies.
Down‑arrow button that appears at fold height, smoothly scrolling users to the next content block.
Prominent button that slides in a side drawer of filters, common on mobile catalog pages.
Vertical list of steps with active highlight, guiding users through a multi‑page wizard.
Long‑press on mobile shows a peek preview card; releasing navigates, swiping cancels.
Invisible listener that cycles focus to next/previous sections with Ctrl + Arrow keys.
Tiny “×” button inside tags or pills that deletes the item without extra dialogs.
Narrow horizontal bar that appears on hover over table rows, exposing edit, view, duplicate icons.
Two small arrow buttons allowing instant scroll to page start or end.
Mobile gesture that dismisses full‑screen modals by swiping down.
Arrow buttons appear when tab labels exceed width, letting users scroll the tab strip.
Fixed vertical stack of dots on the right; clicking a dot scrolls to its corresponding section.
Microphone icon that opens speech recognition, executing commands based on spoken keywords.
Keyboard‑focusable link that jumps directly to the footer, complementing “Skip to Content.”
Users click and drag a rectangle to multi‑select items, triggering a bulk‑actions toolbar.
Prevents accidental destructive actions by requiring users to press and hold until a ring completes.
Top navigation hides when scrolling down to maximize content and reappears when scrolling up.
Small movable bubble displaying current heading title; clicking opens an index of all sections.
